Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dextrocardia (heart apex pointing to the right) and a left-sided horizontal fissure, which are radiographic hallmarks of situs inversus. This anatomical reversal, combined with the clinical history of sinusitis and recurrent respiratory infections (suggesting underlying bronchiectasis/primary ciliary dyskinesia), confirms the diagnosis of Kartagener syndrome.
